stem.en: Kabir says "crossing over is a mistake, like a mutation; the chromosome ends up mixed up". What is the difference?

text.en: A mutation changes a letter. Crossing over swaps matching stretches between two chromosomes that carry the same genes in the same order, so no letter is changed and no gene is lost; the spellings are recombined. It is a regular step of the dance, done on purpose by enzymes.
No difference; both scramble the tape.

feedback.en: Crossing over keeps every gene in place with a different partner spelling beside it. The tape reads perfectly. Only the combination is new.

text.en: Crossing over is a mutation that happens to help.

feedback.en: It is not a mistake. Enzymes cut and rejoin the pair at matching points, every meiosis, in every sexual organism.

text.en: Crossing over only happens in peas.

feedback.en: It happens in you, the moong and yeast. Mendel never knew of it.

explanation.en: Mutation makes new spellings. Crossing over and random line-up make new combinations of existing spellings. Both make variation; only one is an error.
